scenes.heading: Molecular genetics
scenes.sub: How DNA is copied, read and controlled
scenes.say: Mendel described what is inherited. Molecular genetics explains how. DNA is copied, read out as RNA, then made into protein. And cells control which genes are read, and when.

scenes.heading: DNA replication
points: Semi-conservative: one old, one new strand
Help Stop That Primer, Please Link
scenes.say: Replication is semi-conservative: each new helix keeps one old strand. DNA polymerase only adds to a free three prime end, so new DNA always grows five prime to three prime. The leading strand is continuous. The lagging strand is made in short Okazaki fragments, joined by ligase.
scenes.caption: Replication is semi-conservative: each new helix keeps one old strand. DNA polymerase only adds to a free 3′ end, so new DNA always grows 5′ → 3′. The leading strand is continuous. The lagging strand is made in short Okazaki fragments, joined by ligase.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cutting a highlights reel from a full footy match
scenes.science: Splicing removes introns and joins exons in mRNA
scenes.breaks: Introns aren't just boring footage: some help control the gene, and cuts must be exact to the nucleotide or the reading frame shifts.
scenes.say: The full match recording, the DNA, stays safe in the nucleus. RNA polymerase makes a working copy. Editors cut out the bits that won't make the reel, the introns, and join the exons. That's splicing. Choosing different clips gives different reels: alternative splicing.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Template strand: 3′-TAC GGA TTC ACT-5′. What polypeptide is made?
lines: AUG = Met, CCU = Pro, AAG = Lys
scenes.say: The template reads T A C, G G A, T T C, A C T. The m R N A is complementary: A U G, C C U, A A G, U G A. Translate: methionine, proline, lysine, then a stop codon. So the polypeptide is Met, Pro, Lys.
scenes.caption: The template reads TAC GGA TTC ACT. The mRNA is complementary: AUG CCU AAG UGA. Translate: methionine, proline, lysine, then a stop codon. So the polypeptide is Met–Pro–Lys.

scenes.heading: Mutations: mildest to worst
scenes.say: Mutations run from mildest to usually worst. Silent: same amino acid. Missense: a different amino acid. Nonsense: an early stop codon. Frameshift: an insertion or deletion that scrambles every codon after it. But adding or removing three bases doesn't shift the frame.

scenes.heading: The lac operon
points: Fully on: lactose present, glucose absent
scenes.say: Bacteria switch on the lac operon only when they need it. Lactose lifts the lock: it pulls the repressor off the operator. Low glucose lights the lamp: c A M P binds CAP and boosts transcription. So it's fully on only with lactose present and glucose absent.
scenes.caption: Bacteria switch on the lac operon only when they need it. Lactose lifts the lock: it pulls the repressor off the operator. Low glucose lights the lamp: cAMP binds CAP and boosts transcription. So it's fully on only with lactose present and glucose absent.

points: Pre-mRNA is capped, tailed and spliced
mRNA copies the coding strand (U for T)
scenes.say: Quick recap. Replication is semi-conservative and always five prime to three prime. Eukaryotic pre-m R N A is capped, tailed and spliced. Mutations range from silent to frameshift. The lac operon needs lactose and no glucose. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Replication is semi-conservative and always 5′ → 3′. Eukaryotic pre-mRNA is capped, tailed and spliced. Mutations range from silent to frameshift. The lac operon needs lactose and no glucose. Now try the practice questions!
